column1: Combat|Fight on cleared ground with room to retreat, not in a cramped kitchen.
Combat|Separate a small encounter from the crowd before you commit to swinging.
Combat|Leave a gap behind you; backing into a wall can end a controlled fight.
Combat|A shove can buy space when a zombie gets inside your weapon's reach.
Combat|Check behind you between encounters, even on a street you cleared earlier.
Combat|Fence crossings can knock zombies down, but their lunges are still dangerous.
Combat|Carry a usable backup weapon before your main one reaches breaking point.
Combat|Learn your weapon's reach against isolated targets, not a surrounding crowd.
Combat|If swings become ineffective, retreat and check your condition before retrying.
Combat|Do not let a finishing stomp distract you from a second approaching zombie.
Escape|Healthy survivors can often walk away from shamblers; sprinters change that.
Escape|Save your sprint for a closing gap instead of spending it on routine travel.
Escape|Break sight, then change direction; one corner is not proof you lost pursuit.
Escape|Scout the far side of a fence before making it your escape route.
Escape|Heavy loads can spoil a fence escape. Leave room in your carrying budget.
Escape|Crouching reduces your profile; it does not make you invisible up close.
Escape|A dense forest can hide your pursuers and your next obstacle. Plan ahead.
Escape|Know where you will retreat before you attract a group away from loot.
Escape|Avoid sprinting through clutter when a clear street offers another route.
Escape|A blocked escape route is a reason to abandon the loot objective.
Condition|Sleepiness and exertion are different problems; a short rest is not sleep.
Condition|Read a new moodle's tooltip before you decide to keep fighting.
Condition|Build 42 muscle strain is a reason to shorten fights and change activities.
Condition|Rest somewhere secure before low endurance becomes an emergency.
Condition|Check clothing and temperature when your survivor keeps overheating.
Condition|A bigger backpack does not remove the risks of an overloaded survivor.
Condition|Return trips need energy too. Start heading home before you are spent.
Condition|Schedule exercise before a recovery period, not before a dangerous raid.
Condition|Pain and injuries can explain poor combat even when your weapon is sound.
Condition|Choose today's job around your condition instead of yesterday's plan.
Loot|Give each trip a short shopping list so low-value loot does not bury it.
Loot|A working weapon, drinking water and bandages matter more than rare trophies.
Loot|Keep emergency supplies accessible instead of buried in a bag on the floor.
Loot|Equipped bags reduce carried item weight, but their reduction is not unlimited.
Loot|Leave some capacity for the item you actually came to find.
Loot|Mark promising buildings and return prepared rather than taking everything.
Loot|Check nearby rooms before settling into a long inventory transfer.
Loot|A flashlight and spare batteries make darkness a smaller surprise.
Loot|Prioritize tools for your next project instead of hoarding every duplicate.
Loot|Keep a small return-home supply separate from loot you plan to discard.
Shelter|Check every room before calling a building your safe place to sleep.
Shelter|Cover exposed windows before turning a temporary shelter into home.
Shelter|Choose a fallback exit before barricading your main entrance.
Shelter|A sheet-rope exit can be torn down. Recheck it before relying on it.
Shelter|Remove remaining window glass before using that opening as a route.
Shelter|A quiet location can be worth more than a large building full of storage.
Shelter|Keep a second refuge stocked in case your main shelter becomes unsafe.
Shelter|Do not assume a tall fence makes the whole property permanently safe.
Shelter|Store an emergency kit where you can reach it without crossing the house.
Shelter|Keep your entrance and escape path clear of your own stored clutter.
Water|Fill useful containers while the taps work instead of waiting for shutoff.
Water|Check the water's contamination label before drinking from a new source.
Water|Rain collection supplies water, not a promise of drinkable water.
Water|Treat tainted water and confirm its status has changed before drinking.
Water|Use a suitable cooking container when boiling a batch of unsafe water.
Water|Keep a clean reserve for travel rather than carrying only untreated water.
Water|Do not assume plumbing has purified the water arriving at a sink.
Water|A renewable water source still needs a safe collection and treatment route.
Water|Refill before a long journey; finding an empty bottle is not finding water.
Water|Check auto-drink settings and keep your drinking container accessible.
Food|Use perishables while they are fresh and keep a shelf-stable reserve.
Food|A powered freezer slows spoilage; plan for the day that power stops.
Food|Check food condition before eating an item left behind on an old trip.
Food|Watch the cooking progress instead of leaving a meal on a running stove.
Food|Switch cooking appliances off before you leave the shelter.
Food|A full stomach and a stable body weight are not the same thing.
Food|Watch your weight trend when living on a narrow range of foods.
Food|Carry a way to open the canned food you pack for a journey.
Food|Check the actual recipe for preservation supplies before harvesting a surplus.
Food|Keep spare food while learning farming or fishing; a new system takes time.
Wounds|Get out of immediate danger, then stop bleeding before resuming your trip.
Wounds|Keep spare clean bandages on your character, not only in your vehicle.
Wounds|Inspect the Health panel after an injury instead of guessing what happened.
Wounds|An ordinary wound-infection label is not a diagnosis of the Knox virus.
Wounds|Do not treat disinfectant as a cure for zombie transmission.
Wounds|Check footwear before crossing broken glass or rough ground.
Wounds|Inspect damaged clothing; old protection ratings may no longer apply.
Wounds|Treat an injured hand or leg as a change to your combat or travel plan.
Wounds|Choose a secure treatment location before starting a longer medical action.
Wounds|Replenish your first-aid kit after a close call, not during the next one.
Vehicles|Inspect fuel, battery and engine condition before betting your escape on a car.
Vehicles|Check tires and hood condition as well as whether the engine starts.
Vehicles|Park with a clear departure route rather than facing a wall or a crowd.
Vehicles|Slow down before blind corners and wrecks, not after they fill the screen.
Vehicles|Keep a small emergency kit on your person in case you must abandon the car.
Vehicles|Repeated zombie impacts damage the vehicle you depend on for transport.
Vehicles|A noisy engine can bring company to the place where you stop.
Vehicles|Make sure the side you plan to exit is clear before leaving your seat.
Vehicles|Keep fuel resupply in your route plan before you explore farther afield.
Vehicles|Inspect your car again after a collision, even if it still drives.
Crafting|Use the current crafting search instead of relying on an old recipe list.
Crafting|Check required skills, tools and work surfaces before hauling materials home.
Crafting|Some recipes need a hard surface nearby; loose ingredients are not enough.
Crafting|Read recipe literature when you find it, then confirm what it unlocked.
Crafting|Store project supplies together so a missing small item is easy to spot.
Crafting|Choose one useful project before trying to learn every crafting branch.
Crafting|Check a recipe's output before spending scarce ingredients on a substitute.
Crafting|Keep a serviceable tool in reserve when a project depends on that tool.
Crafting|Use recovery time for reading or planning instead of another long fight.
Crafting|Recheck requirements after an update; Build 41 instructions may no longer fit.
Power and fire|Run generators outdoors; opening an indoor window is not a safety plan.
Power and fire|Learn the current generator requirements before the electricity fails.
Power and fire|Plan both fuel and maintenance supplies before depending on a generator.
Power and fire|A generator adds noise as well as power. Consider what is nearby.
Power and fire|Keep an independent light source for a power failure or a fuel shortage.
Power and fire|Make water and food plans that still function without refrigeration.
Power and fire|Do not use a fire-clearing tactic beside the shelter you need to preserve.
Power and fire|Check burning appliances and fires before sleeping or leaving the area.
Power and fire|Store critical supplies in more than one place in case fire destroys a base.
Power and fire|Keep a clear path away from a fire instead of trapping yourself behind it.
Long term|Check a crop's current planting information before spending your seeds.
Long term|Keep food reserves while crops mature; planting does not feed you tonight.
Long term|Plan animal feed and water before bringing livestock back to your base.
Long term|Inspect animal water supplies before leaving on a long expedition.
Long term|Farming, animals and exploration compete for time. Grow your workload slowly.
Long term|Balance clothing protection with heat and movement for the job ahead.
Long term|Recheck nearby threats when returning from a trip; yesterday's path can change.
Long term|Read your sandbox settings; advice for shamblers may fail with sprinters.
Long term|Treat a modded mechanic as something to check, not a vanilla guarantee.
Long term|If a plan costs your escape route, change the plan before the zombies do.
